title: First Draft: 🚓👮 Guess Who's Afraid of Going to Jail?
author: Asawin Suebsaeng
content:
_On this day in 1962, the great Walter Cronkite began anchoring 'CBS Evening
News' - a role that helped define him as "the most trusted man in America."
Under Bari Weiss's leadership, the program and network have since been turned
into a soft MAGA mouthpiece._

Good morning! It's **Swin** again. In a classic 1994 episode of 'The Simpsons'
(the TV series that nearly three decades ago
["predicted"](https://www.thedailybeast.com/simpsons-writer-trump-
presidential-run-not-as-fun-as-it-should-be/) a disastrous **Donald Trump**
presidency), **Homer Simpson** seizes on a [crime
panic](https://zeteo.com/p/how-the-media-makes-you-more-afraid) and [crumbling
trust in institutions](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-
features/trump-inauguration-2024-win-democrats-failed-1235241327/), and forms
a neighborhood watch to patrol Springfield's streets and enforce vigilante
justice. When the local TV newsman asks Homer about the "accusation that your
group has been causing more crimes than it's been preventing," Homer
[responds](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D1ELuUzct3A): "I'd be lying if I
said my men weren't committing crimes."

That was fiction - but it also sums up Donald Trump's entire second term, thus
far. As Trump and his gang break so many laws and commit so many
([war](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-hegseth-admin-lawyers-warn-boat-strike-
illegal)) crimes, do they feel invincible? We can answer that for you…

In today's '**First Draft** ,' Team Trump worries that preemptive pardons
won't be enough to get away with all their crimes; 40 Senate Democrats just
voted to block arms sales to Israel; and **Abdul El-Sayed** picks up a key
endorsement in Michigan's Democratic primary for US Senate.

# Fearing Accountability

They can [read a poll](https://zeteo.com/p/are-these-trumps-worst-poll-
numbers-first-draft). They won't admit it publicly, but much of President
Donald Trump's inner circle sees Democrats retaking the House in the 2026
midterms as a foregone conclusion. They also know, at some point in the near
future, their liberal enemies will control the White House, again.

And Team Trump takes it for granted that there will be an intense appetite
among progressive voters for their politicians to go on their own
**"[retribution](https://zeteo.com/p/institutionalizing-revenge-miles-
taylor)"** tour and seek accountability for all of this administration's
[extrajudicial killings](https://zeteo.com/p/donald-trump-ice-occupation-
minnesota) and [crime-doing](https://zeteo.com/p/second-strike-all-of-the-us-
strikes).

As **[Zeteo](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-is-already-discussing-preemptive)**[
reported in December](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-is-already-discussing-
preemptive), the president has already privately discussed preemptive mass
federal pardons before this term ends, to gift an extra layer of impunity to
his rogues' gallery of staff and hatchetmen. Last week, the _Wall Street
Journal_ [followed up](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/trump-promises-
mass-pardons-to-staff-before-leaving-office-d7274d32) on Trump's **"
promise"** to do this.

Last year, various Trump administration officials made sure to purchase new
legal insurance and professional-liability plans, sources familiar with the
matter tell me, in anticipation of future investigations or subpoenas from
prosecutors and Democrats. (It's a smart move: Staffers on the House committee
investigating Jan. 6 [did the same
thing](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/jan-6-committee-
republican-revenge-1234646303/) before the 2022 elections, anticipating a
Republican-run Congress around the corner.)

But in the past few months (including during Trump's disastrous war in Iran,
which has turbo-charged the levels of leaking, backbiting, blame-shifting, and
paranoia [within Team Trump's own ranks](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-huge-hunt-
leakers-nyt)), I've noticed something.

In my conversations with several senior administration officials, as well as
other Trump advisers and elite Republicans close to the White House, their
anxiety - over what Democrats might do to them after the midterms, or once
Trump is out of power - has kicked up a conspicuous notch. Some of them have
told me they've noticed a growing trend of Democratic politicians making
public calls for aggressive prosecutions of Trumplanders in the future - a
trend one Trump aide privately lamented as **" kind of worrisome."**

And a significant number of senior appointees working in Pete Hegseth's
Pentagon, in Stephen Miller's White House, and in so many other departments
and crime-laboratories of the Trump-Vance administration do not think that
federal pardons will be enough.
